title: Inside Calculo Capital- Crushing Commodity Markets with Machine Learning - Open Interest 15

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Inside Calculo Capital- Crushing Commodity Markets with Machine Learning - Open Interest 15.docx

speakers: Ola Hansen (Saxo Bank commodity strategist, Calculo board member)
summary: Interview with Calculo Capital, a Copenhagen short-term (2 to 5 day) systematic commodity CTA. Classical breakout trend-following entries, machine learning used only for exits via pattern matching to historical trades; plus Saxo's commodity outlook for early 2025 (precious metals, tariffs, natural gas).

coverage.note: Teaser of ML matching, disclaimers, host intro of Calculo and fund profile
Commodity market review early 2025; precious metals; long-term themes (deglobalisation, defence)
Energy transition, demographics, mining supply, softs, natural gas, Calculo gas trade
Copper, COMEX tariff premium, physical flows, silver
Calculo focus on commodities, holding period, liquidity, supply shocks
Entry signals, ML risk management, hurricane example, price-only inputs
Flat positions, exit methodology, ML matching, daily bars
Trend-only entries, ML for exit only
Execution timing, why Ola invests, BCOM drawdowns
Index design, roll yield, track record

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - Calculo's method and Ola's outlook are well covered; missed the China-tariff copper driver, ML-noise caveat, no-curve design point, index composition and broad backwardation, and misattributed the host's natural gas trade to Calculo

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: Third, because they are short-term withholding periods of 1 to 10 days per trade.
claims.claim: Calculo Capital is a Copenhagen systematic CTA that trades only commodities with 1 to 10 day holding periods and uses machine learning in its trading process.
claims.testable: partly - strategy description, not a testable claim itself

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: I watch something like the Bloomberg commodity index which uh which is broadly exposed to agricultural com metals and energy and it's up nearly 10%
claims.claim: The Bloomberg Commodity Index was up almost 10% in the first weeks of 2025, ahead of equities, with all sectors posting gains.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: that really is just an expression of an a world that is not in balance.
claims.claim: Strong demand for gold and other precious metals, which yield nothing and cost money to store, is a hedge against an uncertain, unbalanced world.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: Not only central banks who have been buying for the past three years in order to diversify their
claims.claim: Central banks buying gold for three years to diversify away from US dollar assets (plus private investors) is a persistent source of gold demand.
claims.testable: yes - central bank gold purchases are published

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: the fiscal debt worries that uh that that basically comes with the the rising debt burdens we're seeing around the world
claims.claim: Rising government debt burdens, especially in the US, push investors into precious metals as a fiscal-risk hedge.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: we're seeing the the deglobalization where production is being moved closer to home.
claims.claim: Deglobalisation moves production closer to home, which needs a lot of commodities and could raise some prices.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: We have the increased spending on defense coming through in Europe now in a in a big way.
claims.claim: Rising European defence spending requires steel and rare-earth minerals, supporting commodity demand.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: the energy transition is also a question of of we're moving towards increased use of power and it's not only towards electrical vehicles it's also towards data centers
claims.claim: The energy transition raises power demand (EVs, data centers, cooling), so it supports copper, aluminium, lithium, cobalt, nickel and silver.
claims.direction: copper, aluminium, lithium, cobalt, nickel, silver up

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: the money that we are saved in over decades that's that will be spent
claims.claim: An ageing population with accumulated savings will spend that money, adding to consumption and commodity demand.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: urbanization undergoing in especially in emerging markets that will also underpin the demand.
claims.claim: Continuing urbanisation in emerging markets underpins commodity demand.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: mining companies they have to look 10 to 12 years out and try to gauge what the price would be out there.
claims.claim: Mining projects take many years, so miners must guess prices 10 to 12 years ahead, which holds back investment and can cause future metal shortfalls.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: making them much more exposed to any weather developments.
claims.claim: Softs are produced in small geographic areas, so weather in West Africa (cocoa) and Brazil (coffee) drives large price moves.
claims.indicator: weather in cocoa and coffee regions

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: US exports of gas is rising. US demand for gas as well is also rising and that will over time underpin prices.
claims.claim: Rising US gas exports, domestic demand and European LNG demand underpin a long-term bullish case for natural gas.
claims.indicator: US natural gas exports and demand

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: We got kicked out of a short Henry hop position which we've had on for more than two years.
claims.claim: Calculo's short Henry Hub natural gas trade, held more than two years, was exited by a rally on 20 February 2025 after a cold weather outlook, an example of a trend position ending only when the trend reverses.

correction.issue: wrong speaker and fund: the two-year short Henry Hub trade belongs to host Moritz Seibert's long-term trend fund, not Calculo (whose holding period is 2 to 5 days)
correction.fix: Moritz Seibert: his trend-following fund's short Henry Hub position, held more than two years, was stopped out by the late-February 2025 rally on a colder weather outlook, an example of a long-held trend ending on reversal.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: we're seeing right now that futures prices for gold, silver, copper, platinum, they have all been uh been
claims.claim: Tariff worries lifted US COMEX futures prices of gold, silver, copper and platinum above London spot prices because imported metal would face tariffs.
claims.conditions: While tariff threat on metals persists

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: if you have access to physicals and you can sell the future against it, you are earning a handsome handsome return.
claims.claim: The COMEX-London premium made it profitable to ship physical gold and silver to New York and sell futures against it, drawing in large inventories; the cash and carry basis on gold was about 10% annualised.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: then there's a lot of physical gold sitting in the US uh with no uh end user.
claims.claim: When the premium narrows, physical gold in US vaults with no end user may be sold or hedged, a possible small negative for prices.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: the de demand in China has held up phenomenally well even though the construction
claims.claim: Chinese copper demand has held up despite the construction downturn, and data centers and power transmission add demand beyond EVs.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: It was the guy who supplied the shovels.
claims.claim: In the gold rush the shovel supplier made the money, so power-grid builders such as Siemens Energy (up 300%) capture the AI and electrification boom, as Nvidia did.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: because if you are if you have a if you're short gold in London market, you can go to the Bank of England and uh and and lease gold from uh from them.
claims.claim: Gold shorts can borrow from the Bank of England but silver has no lender of last resort, so silver gets squeezed harder.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: there's probably more higher risk that tariffs would be added to silver than to gold being a a monetary
claims.claim: Silver carries higher tariff risk than gold because gold is quasi-monetary and much silver comes from Mexico.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: it's more like 2 to 5 days actually.
claims.claim: Calculo holds trades 2 to 5 days: it captures the alpha move and uses AI to choose the exit.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: This fear sparks price movements and these movements is actually what we uh want to capture in our trend following model.
claims.claim: Supply constraints from weather or regional events create fear and price moves, which trend following can capture; this works in commodities and not in equities or rates, which explains the commodities-only focus.
claims.direction: long after upward shock, short after downward
claims.conditions: Works where supply and demand are physically constrained
claims.testable: partly - compare trend returns by asset class

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: we only do trade the liquid stuff.
claims.claim: Calculo trades only the most liquid metals, agriculturals, softs and energies, which also lets it scale.
claims.conditions: Excludes small markets such as orange juice

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: with your trading frequency you're absolutely much more sensitive to that
claims.claim: Shorter-horizon traders are much more sensitive to market liquidity than slow trend followers, who do not need to trade daily.
claims.testable: partly - cost and capacity by horizon

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: Basically we use only uh price patterns as our entry.
claims.claim: Entries are classical CTA breakouts and the advanced part is the post-entry risk management, which aims at low-volatility access to commodities.
claims.direction: long breakout up, short breakout down

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: commodities can be volatile and and it through the use of AI, we can sort out a lot of the volatility and create a more linary return profile.
claims.claim: Machine learning applied to risk management reduces volatility and gives a smoother return profile than plain trend following.
claims.testable: partly - compare with and without ML exit

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: after this initial risk premium being put into the market, the market will look at the hurricane development
claims.claim: A hurricane threat first adds a risk premium (the price jump), then the market waits on the storm path; the system gets signals from price momentum and candlesticks during this limbo.
claims.testable: partly - event study of weather shocks

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: So quite often we do participate in these movements where the market uh stabilizes a bit and trades sideways and this is often enough for us to exit the positions capturing the alpha
claims.claim: After a shock move the market often goes sideways, which is enough for the model to take profit and then re-enter the trend if it resumes.
claims.direction: exit after spike, re-enter on resumption

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: there's no manual input in regards to selecting signals.
claims.claim: The system uses price only, with no weather input and no manual override of signals.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: we only want to participate in in real alpha periods
claims.claim: The model can be flat, partly long or partly short, with no mandatory allocation to any market or sector.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: 75 80% of our trades is handled via the machine learning exits.
claims.claim: About 75 to 80% of trades are closed by machine learning exits and the rest by classical stops and trailing stops.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: when we take this new data put into our database, it finds a match that is as close to something it has seen before.
claims.claim: Each day the open trade's candlestick and momentum features are matched to a database of historical trades with known T+1 and T+2 outcomes, then classified as keep or eliminate.
claims.indicator: nearest-neighbour matching on candlestick and momentum features
claims.direction: exit when matched history shows adverse outcome

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: we try to capture bits and pieces of these existing trends and trying to vet out any counter moves along the way.
claims.claim: Capturing parts of trends and avoiding counter-moves gives a smoother ride but not the whole trend, as classical longer-term CTAs do; ML uses daily bars.
claims.conditions: Trade-off: smoother returns but misses the tail of trends

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: We use trend following strategies to enter the markets. Trend only.
claims.claim: Entries are trend only with no mean reversion.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: I do believe that trends have strength.
claims.claim: Machine learning is not used for entry because predicting where the market moves is a guess; it is used only for exits, where it avoids learning noise about direction.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: we actually only use it as a riskoff element which changes the picture quite a bit compared to trying to build a fully AI model that tries to predict the price targets.
claims.claim: Using ML only as a risk-off element avoids the overfitting problem of price prediction models.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: timed towards the most liquid time in the US.
claims.claim: Machine learning exits are timed at the most liquid hours and are flags of possible correction, not firm predictions, so execution is done in liquid periods.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: We had the two biggest one was a 77 months draw down between 15 and 20 where it fell 38%.
claims.claim: The long-only Bloomberg Commodity Index had a 77-month, 38% drawdown from 2015 to 2020 and a further 22% drop after 2022, so a long/short strategy with similar returns and lower volatility is preferable.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: we had to have bad months for equities we quite often find that uh that there's actually some uh positive months coming in through the commodities.
claims.claim: Commodity strategy returns tend to be positive in bad equity months, lowering portfolio volatility.
claims.indicator: commodity strategy vs equity monthly returns

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: commodities don't have the equity drift or anything like that.
claims.claim: Commodities have no equity-like positive drift, so they should be traded both long and short.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: because it's a relatively small market, is not a BCOM member.
claims.claim: Cocoa was not in the Bloomberg Commodity Index because of its size, so the index missed the cocoa rally, while natural gas, a member, dragged it down.

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: there was a massive re rebalancing in in the when January came because the the percentage share of expos exposure to coco out of the total was uh had gone quite extreme
claims.claim: Index rebalancing in January forced sales of a winner whose weight had grown extreme (cocoa).

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: I don't find them having been particularly successful uh they haven't really outperformed uh the uh the main uh total return in in the indices.
claims.claim: Smart-roll commodity ETFs have not outperformed the main total return indices.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: you have been making money being short simply on the the role of the uh the role from a from a from a low to a high contract.
claims.claim: In contango, a short position earns roll yield (natural gas); Calculo benefited from the upward-sloping curve but does not roll monthly and is aware of seasonality.

correction.issue: wrong attribution: the natural gas short that earned contango roll yield is Seibert's fund, not Calculo; Ola raised the roll point and Seibert replied
correction.fix: Ola Hansen / Moritz Seibert: in contango a short natural gas position earned roll yield even through big rallies; Seibert's fund benefited from the upward-sloping curve, though it does not roll every month and watches seasonality.

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: that we over the past seven years almost since inception has actually delivered equity-like returns at 2/3 of the volatility of uh the broad stock indices.
claims.claim: Calculo reports equity-like returns at two-thirds of stock index volatility since 2018, non-correlated and non-cyclical.
claims.testable: partly - track record claim, not verified

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: I think first of foremost the fact that uh that that China hasn't been slapped with terrorists just yet. Uh that's probably one thing
claims.claim: Copper's early-2025 rally (about 15%) is driven first by China not yet being hit with US tariffs, alongside tariff-driven dislocations in COMEX pricing.
claims.indicator: US tariff decisions on China; copper price
claims.direction: copper up while China escapes tariffs
claims.conditions: until tariffs on China are imposed
claims.testable: partly - copper moves around China tariff announcements

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: how do you prevent the machine to learn from the noise which is you know a prevalent factor in the markets.
claims.claim: Machine learning applied to market prediction risks fitting noise, and Seibert jokes that a clever machine would probably just rediscover buying breakouts, i.e. become a trend follower.
claims.indicator: ML model trained on price data
claims.conditions: noisy market data; ML used for direction prediction
claims.testable: partly - compare ML entry rules with plain breakout rules out of sample

claims.speaker: Philip Engel Carlson
claims.quote: Does this information trigger anything at Calculu or are you maybe even trading spreads uh which you know you can do in the commodity markets? is when we're not trading spreads as no.
claims.claim: Calculo does not use forward-curve information (contango, backwardation, seasonality) as a signal and does not trade calendar spreads; only outright futures on price patterns.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert
claims.quote: the first [L380] generation of these indices, they're equity and metals heavy. And then there's all the, you know, smart variations that um are more diversified and they distribute liquidity across the curve more.
claims.claim: First-generation long-only commodity indices (e.g. BCOM) are concentrated (caption says equity; likely energy) and metals heavy and exclude small markets, while newer variants diversify more and spread exposure along the curve, so index choice drives commodity beta returns.
claims.indicator: commodity index composition and curve placement
claims.testable: yes - compare first-generation vs diversified/curve-spread indices

claims.speaker: Ola Hansen
claims.quote: we generally are starting to see a a positive royal coming into the markets except uh and the big exception is is obviously where you just have had your profitable short in natural gas
claims.claim: Roll yield has turned positive (backwardation) across most commodity markets, with US natural gas the big exception where contango kept rewarding shorts even through price spikes.
claims.indicator: futures curve slope / roll yield by commodity
claims.direction: long backwardated markets earn roll; short contango natural gas earns roll
claims.conditions: backwardated curves (most markets) vs contango (natural gas)
claims.testable: yes - curve slope and roll returns by market
